concepts.label: durable write
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the general server-side write-durability mechanism the round-12 brief flagged as absent. Deliberately NOT the same concept as sdk:transaction-durability (a single DurabilityLevel setting scoped to one SDK transaction attempt); this page describes the underlying general mechanism that ordinary per-key-value writes, not just transactions, use. See cross_component_finding.

concepts.label: regular write
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the asynchronous, no-guarantee counterpart to durability:durable-write, named explicitly on the page.

concepts.label: Durability Level
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - modeled as a ConceptScheme with a flat literal list, same pattern as index-state and eventing:function-lifecycle-state, since the page itself frames it as one settable parameter with 'valid settings'.

concepts.label: majority (Durability Level)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - member of durability:level; promoted to its own id rather than left as a bare literal because the page states a bucket-type compatibility fact specific to this one value.

concepts.label: majorityAndPersistActive (Durability Level)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - member of durability:level, restricted to Couchbase buckets per the page.

concepts.label: persistToMajority (Durability Level)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - member of durability:level, restricted to Couchbase buckets per the page.

concepts.label: majority requirement
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the node-count-for-majority mechanism (a table keyed by replica count), distinct from the Level *value* called 'majority' - every durability level, not just the one literally named 'majority', must satisfy this requirement.

concepts.label: durability timeout
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the second of the two durability parameters (Level, Timeout) the page names explicitly.

concepts.label: SYNC_WRITE_IN_PROGRESS
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the status Couchbase Server returns when a client attempts to write a key that already has a durable write pending.

concepts.label: ambiguous result
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the outcome reported when Couchbase Server cannot confirm whether a durable write succeeded (timeout, node/network failure, rebalance interaction).

concepts.label: durabilityImpossibleFallback setting
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the bucket-level escape-hatch setting that reports durable-write success even when the majority is unreachable, at the explicit cost of the durability guarantee.

concepts.label: maxCount (sequential auto-failover limit)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the auto-failover setting used to protect durable writes from being lost to cascading automatic failovers.

concepts.label: auto-failover preserve durable writes setting
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a global Enterprise-only setting limiting automatic failover of Data Service nodes to protect durability; sibling/alternative to durability:max-count-setting.

concepts.label: Couchbase bucket (type)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - new topical namespace for the on-prem bucket-type axis (Couchbase vs Ephemeral), distinct from capella:bucket (Capella's data-hierarchy concept) and from cloud-provider:* (deployment substrate, not bucket type).

concepts.label: Ephemeral bucket (type)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - sibling of bucket-type:couchbase; memory-only bucket type that cannot use durability levels requiring persistence to disk.

concepts.label: vBucket
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the active/replica data-partition unit this page constantly refers to (active vBucket, replica vBucket) when explaining durable-write mechanics; not previously in the server: family alongside server:node/server:rebalance.

concepts.label: failover
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - general concept for manual/automatic node failover; kept deliberately coarse here (this page treats failover only as a threat to durability guarantees) and links out via seeAlso to the dedicated failover.md / automatic-failover.md pages rather than modeling graceful/hard/automatic as separate concepts, since those pages are outside this batch.

notable_absence.finding: No RBAC privilege is named anywhere on this page for setting or overriding durability requirements, even though the page describes both client-side and bucket-side configuration paths ('Either or both the client and the bucket can set durability requirements'). Every other configuration surface in the registry that lets a client override a server default is usually paired with a privilege or role check; this one is not, at least not on this page.

cross_component_finding: This page fills exactly the gap the round-12 brief named: durability:durable-write is the general, non-transaction-scoped write-durability mechanism, and it is genuinely NOT the same concept as sdk:transaction-durability. The registry's existing note on sdk:transaction-durability says it applies 'a single DurabilityLevel setting... to every key-value write inside one transaction attempt' via TransactionsConfig - a transaction-scoped configuration surface. This page's mechanism is the one TransactionsConfig's setting is layered on top of: the same three-level enum (majority / majorityAndPersistActive / persistToMajority) recurs here as the base case, making this now a FOURTH scope for that enum family, alongside the three already flagged in sharesOptionSetWith's note (per-KV-operation via sdk:durability, per-transaction-config via sdk:transaction-durability, per-single-query-transaction-call). I did not add a sharesOptionSetWith relation myself since this page never mentions transactions' durability configuration by name (only the one 'Durability is essential for features like Transactions' sentence) - that link is asserted here only via the new requiresCapability relation, not via sharesOptionSetWith, to avoid inventing a same-enum claim this page doesn't itself state.
cross_product_finding: No Capella, SDK, or Sync Gateway angle on this page - it is pure Couchbase Server KV-engine mechanics (vBuckets, Data Service nodes, REST API/CLI configuration). The only forward reference is to n1ql:transactions, which is itself Server-scoped.
